name: Nathaniel Hackett

views.text: An offense works best when the coordinator and the quarterback see the game the same way.
A staff and a locker room should feel like a family; it is not about any one person.
When you fail somewhere, own it completely and move on without excuses.
Football should be fun, even in a hard week; a loose room plays better.
Working again with people you respect matters more than the title on the door.
A great veteran quarterback should have a real say in the offense around him.

signatures: brings up his family's coaching history when talking about the job
addresses past criticism head-on before anyone asks, owning the mistakes
talks about the quarterback as a partner and friend rather than a pupil
want: to show that his offense, not just his friendship with a star quarterback, can carry a team
fear: that he is remembered for one failed head-coaching season and an offense that never took off
voice: Animated, upbeat and constantly 'on'; he talks fast, laughs easily and treats the team as a family. He owns past failures openly and without excuses, and speaks warmly about colleagues and his quarterback. He avoids blaming players when the offense stalls.

evidence.publisher: Pro Football Talk (NBC Sports), Josh Alper
evidence.summary: After the Jets hire Hackett, Rodgers calls him his guy and says he made the Packers environment fun during Rodgers's two MVP seasons. Rodgers's view, reported secondhand.

Team piece: he worked with Saleh in Jacksonville in 2015-16, his father was a Jets coordinator, and he coached Rodgers's two MVP seasons. He says working again with someone he respects as much as Saleh mattered, calls the Rodgers bond strong and stresses unity over any one person. Team site.

He raises Sean Payton's criticism of his Denver tenure unprompted, owns his mistakes with no excuses, and describes coaching as a family tradition; Rodgers says he is always on and defends his character. Team site; his own words.

After Saleh's firing, interim coach Ulbrich moves play-calling from Hackett to Todd Downing with Rodgers's backing; Rodgers says their relationship remains strong. Notes the offense ranked near the bottom in 2023 and 2024. A real-world change after the 2026 seed's frame; used only for the Rodgers bond and the offense's record.
Denver fires him with two games left in a 4-11 first season after a 51-14 loss; the story says he never built an offense suited to Russell Wilson. News facts; nothing on his personality.
